Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

be supposed to phrase

be expected or meant to

also supposed to, not supposed to, you were supposed to, be meant to, was meant to

classical

Plaut. Cas. 765–766: cēnam jam esse coctam oportuit
Ter. Heaut. 536: haec facta ab illō oportēbat

oportet, oportēre, oportuit

verb, second conjugation, impersonal, with an infinitive or an accusative and infinitive

it is right, one should; what is expected

What was supposed to happen and did not: oportuit or oportēbat, in comedy often with a perfect passive infinitive (Plautus, Terence). “Not supposed to”, not allowed, is nōn licet (see allow).

Examples

  • quīn agitis hodiē? quīn datis, sī quid datis? properāte, cēnam jam esse coctam oportuit.

    Come on, get moving! Hand it over, if you’re handing anything! Hurry: dinner was supposed to be ready by now.Plaut. Cas. 765–766

  • Haec facta ab illō oportēbat, Syre.

    That is what he ought to have done, Syrus.Ter. Heaut. 536

  • nōn dēbēmus dēlicātī esse; ubīque medius caelus est

    we mustn’t be fussy; the sky is the same everywherePetr. 45.1

Other words

  • dēbeō, dēbēre, dēbuī, dēbitum — ought, be bound to (a duty)

    verb, second conjugation, with an infinitive · also used · classical · Petr. 45.1: nōn dēbēmus dēlicātī esse; Plin. Ep. 8.16.5: plūra fortasse quam dēbuī

    Of duty or obligation (Lewis & Short: classical prose uses it of moral necessity); for what had to happen of necessity, necesse est.

See also allow.

SourcesLewis & Short: oportet · Lewis & Short: debeo
